research_question: Does requiring both an observable correction reference and one unique explicit response-policy replacement improve linkage to the immediately pending prediction without turning ordinary multilingual negation into correction?
intervention: M38 target-guarded multiscript linkage classifier and canonical feedback adapter
baseline: frozen pre-M38 observe_next_turn feedback linkage behavior
controls: identical pending prediction and feedback input
no model generation call for the linkage mechanism
raw feedback excluded from persisted adaptive store
M37 typed trigger relation behavior unchanged

reserve.source_disjoint_rule: No feedback_input may equal an M36 feedback_input after whitespace and punctuation normalization.
reserve.annotation_rule: A contradicted row must identify exactly one replacement policy different from the pending policy. Ordinary negation and targetless rejection must remain uncertain and unlinked.

operational_definition.correction_reference: observable language that rejects or revises the prior response, not merely a negated proposition
operational_definition.unique_replacement: exactly one of listen_presence, solve_regulation, share_arousal, or playful_tease is explicitly requested
operational_definition.linked_contradiction: pending prediction exists, correction reference is present, unique replacement is present, and replacement differs from the pending policy
operational_definition.fail_closed: missing pending prediction, no replacement, multiple replacement policies, or ordinary proposition negation yields uncertain and unlinked

evidence_boundary: Passing establishes a bounded observable feedback-linkage mechanism, not private intent truth, natural Japanese quality, felt-understanding, or open-domain discourse correction.
